title: Repeated-build evidence record, v1
description: The MEASURED outcome of building the same declared inputs more than once. This is the only document in the repository allowed to say a field is stable across rebuilds. policies/reproducibility.yaml may claim a guarantee over a field only if a record of this shape reports that field `stable`; scripts/repro-guarantees.sh enforces that, so a claim can never outrun its measurement. `not-observed` is a distinct result from `stable` on purpose — the failure this guards against is a comparison that could not see a field reporting no difference and being read as agreement.

guarantee.description: Which of the four guarantees this record is evidence for. Exactly one; a record that spoke to several would be the conflation the whole design exists to prevent.

method.description: How the repetition was controlled, in enough detail to repeat it. A record that does not say whether the builds shared a cache is not evidence: a cached second build compares an image against its own cache and always agrees.

build_count.description: At least two. One build is not a comparison.

declared_inputs_lock_sha256.description: Digest of the build-input lock these builds were run from, with the volatile `generated_at` removed. Binds the measurement to the exact declared inputs; a record cannot be carried over to a different input set.

fields.description: One entry per compared field. Fields are named by the lock path they correspond to, so a policy claim and its evidence refer to the same thing by the same name.

result.description: stable — compared and identical. differs — compared and not identical. not-observed — NOT compared, for any reason. Absence of a difference that was never looked for is not stability.
